iterations.theme: Stephan Lupino: od Rima i New Yorka do lupinizma – fotografija, umjetnost, slava i hrvatski mentalitet

sections.subtitle: Čovjek s više od deset imena: Lupino, Štef, Panča, Ivica…
sections.screenshot_description: Stephan Lupino kroz smijeh nabraja svoje brojne nadimke
sections.content:
Voditelj podcasta **Čušpajz** otvara epizodu predstavljanjem gosta kojeg, kako kaže, mlađe generacije ne treba posebno predstavljati. Uz njega su odrasli, o njemu su čitali i, priznaje voditelj, pomalo mu i zavidjeli. Gost je **Stephan Lupino**, kojeg voditelj predstavlja kao fotografa svjetske klase.

Lupino na to odmah reagira upitnim tonom: fotograf? Njemu je ta etiketa tijesna. Kaže da ljudi od njega stalno traže izložbe fotografija i nove fotografije, a on se danas bavi nečim drugim. Voditelj mu odgovara da ga pamti kao fotografa, ali obećava da će razgovor obuhvatiti i njegov kasniji rad.

Slijedi duhovita epizoda oko oslovljavanja. Voditelj predlaže redom „Štef“, „Stefan“ i „Stjepan“, a Lupino svaki prijedlog odbija dok se ne ustali jednostavno – **Lupino**. Gost se pritom našali i sa slovom „L“, za koje tvrdi da u židovskoj tradiciji znači Bog i da je to njegovo prvo slovo. Neki ga, dodaje, zovu baš tako.

Prema vlastitim riječima, Lupino ima više od deset imena pod kojima ga ljudi znaju. Nabraja ih:
- **Ivan**
- **Štef**
- **Panča**
- **Ivica**
- **Štefina**

Voditelj se slatko nasmije na „Ivicu“, a Lupino zaključuje da ga čak i tako zovu. Uvod tako odmah daje naslutiti razgovor pun humora i osobnih priča.
sections.subtitle_en: A man with more than ten names: Lupino, Štef, Panča, Ivica…
sections.screenshot_description_en: Stephan Lupino through laughter lists his numerous nicknames
sections.content_en:
The host of the podcast **Čušpajz** opens the episode by introducing a guest who, as he says, does not need a special introduction for the younger generations. They grew up with him, read about him, and, the host admits, envied him a little. The guest is **Stephan Lupino**, whom the host introduces as a world-class photographer.

Lupino immediately reacts to this with a questioning tone: a photographer? To him, that label is too tight. He says that people are constantly asking him for photo exhibitions and new photographs, while today he is engaged in something else. The host replies that he remembers him as a photographer, but promises that the conversation will also cover his later work.

A humorous episode follows regarding forms of address. The host suggests in turn "Štef", "Stefan", and "Stjepan", and Lupino rejects each suggestion until simply settling on — **Lupino**. The guest also jokes with the letter "L", which he claims in Jewish tradition means God and that it is his first letter. Some people, he adds, call him just that.

According to his own words, Lupino has more than ten names by which people know him. He lists them:
- **Ivan**
- **Štef**
- **Panča**
- **Ivica**
- **Štefina**

The host laughs heartily at "Ivica", and Lupino concludes that they even call him that. The introduction thus immediately hints at a conversation full of humor and personal stories.

sections.subtitle: Povratak iz Pariza: film o Deborah Turbovel, ženi koja ga je stvorila
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino govori o Deborah Turbovel i dokumentarcu koji se o njoj snima
sections.content:
Lupino se nedavno vratio iz Pariza, gdje je sudjelovao u snimanju dokumentarca o **Deborah Turbovel**. Riječ je o fotografkinji s kojom je radio u New Yorku i koja ga je prva fotografirala. Upravo joj, ističe, duguje to što je postao fotograf. Kasnije ga je, kako kaže, „forsirala“ i inspirirala da postane i umjetnik.

Turbovel je umrla prije sedam godina. O njoj se sada snima veliki film u Americi, a dio i u Parizu, jer je ondje živjela i radila. Lupino napominje da su njih dvoje većinom radili upravo u Parizu. U filmu ima, kako kaže, „dosta jaku ulogu“, što nije čudno s obzirom na to da su se poznavali **35 godina**. Voditelj potvrđuje da mu je gost već poslao neke fotografije sa snimanja.

Odnos s njom Lupino opisuje vrlo emotivno: bila mu je kao sestra i bila mu je sve. Bez obzira na to jesu li bili zajedno ili razdvojeni, uvijek ih je povezivala, kako kaže, posebna „umjetnička vibra“.
sections.subtitle_en: Return from Paris: a film about Deborah Turbeville, the woman who created him
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino speaks about Deborah Turbeville and the documentary being filmed about her
sections.content_en:
Lupino recently returned from Paris, where he participated in filming a documentary about **Deborah Turbovel**. She is a photographer with whom he worked in New York and who was the first to photograph him. It is precisely to her, he points out, that he owes becoming a photographer. Later, as he says, she "pushed" him and inspired him to become an artist as well.

Turbovel died seven years ago. A major film is now being made about her in America, and partly in Paris, because she lived and worked there. Lupino notes that the two of them worked mostly in Paris. In the film, as he says, he has a "fairly strong role", which is not surprising considering that they knew each other for **35 years**. The host confirms that the guest has already sent him some photographs from the shoot.

Lupino describes his relationship with her very emotionally: she was like a sister to him and she was everything to him. Regardless of whether they were together or apart, they were always connected, as he says, by a special "artistic vibe".

sections.subtitle: London bez Engleza i lekcija iz New Yorka: zašto Lupino zagovara različitost
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino uspoređuje nekadašnji i današnji Pariz, London i Rim
sections.content:
Voditelj se dotiče teme koja se, kako kaže, ne može zaobići: koliko su se Europa i Pariz promijenili od Lupinovih mlađih dana. Gost odgovara da u Parizu više ne prepoznaje ni London. Jedino je, prema njegovim riječima, **Rim ostao Rim**.

Velike europske metropole promijenile su se zbog novih populacija. U Londonu se, tvrdi, više ne može vidjeti Englez. Ipak, Lupino tu promjenu ne doživljava negativno, nego je, naprotiv, smatra boljom jer su danas tu ljudi svih rasa. Smatra da bi upravo to trebalo i Hrvatskoj, koja bi tada možda bila puno kreativnija.

Kritizira odnos dijela Hrvata prema stranim radnicima koji dolaze „trbuhom za kruhom“. Podsjeća da smo i sami nekada bili migranti. Voditelj spominje da je Lupino prije nekoliko godina organizirao pomoć za strane radnike, što gost potvrđuje. Dodaje da se kod nas s tim teško nosimo, ali da jedna zemlja ne može biti samo jednog sastava. Kao primjere navodi **Njemačku** i **Francusku**, gdje se to vidi i u nogometnim reprezentacijama.

To je, kaže, odavno shvatio u **New Yorku**, gdje se družio sa svima, od Židova do Arapa. Upravo mu je to iskustvo dalo širu dimenziju. Dodaje i da se danas, pod **Trumpom**, vidi zatvaranje Amerikanaca u sebe. Amerika je velika zemlja i njemu je tada „pasala“, ali danas, smatra, više nije takva.
sections.subtitle_en: London without Englishmen and a lesson from New York: why Lupino advocates diversity
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino compares past and present Paris, London, and Rome
sections.content_en:
The host touches upon a topic that, as he says, cannot be bypassed: how much Europe and Paris have changed since Lupino's younger days. The guest replies that in Paris he no longer recognizes London either. Only, according to his words, **Rome remained Rome**.

Major European metropolises have changed because of new populations. In London, he claims, one can no longer see an Englishman. Nevertheless, Lupino does not perceive this change negatively, but on the contrary, considers it better because today people of all races are there. He considers that this is precisely what Croatia would need as well, which might then be much more creative.

He criticizes the attitude of a portion of Croats toward foreign workers who come "seeking a livelihood". He reminds that we ourselves were once migrants. The host mentions that Lupino organized help for foreign workers a few years ago, which the guest confirms. He adds that among us people have a hard time dealing with this, but that a country cannot be of only one composition. As examples he cites **Germany** and **France**, where this is also seen in national soccer teams.

He says he realized this long ago in **New York**, where he hung out with everyone, from Jews to Arabs. That experience gave him a broader dimension. He also adds that today, under **Trump**, one sees Americans withdrawing into themselves. America is a big country and back then it "suited" him, but today, he believes, it is no longer like that.

sections.subtitle: Rim, karate i noći s kraljem kave: dugi put do Amerike
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino prepričava rimske dane i susret s glumicom Irene Papas
sections.content:
Na pitanje kako je završio u Americi, Lupino odgovara da mu je prva destinacija bio **Rim**, gdje je proveo četiri godine. Bio je učitelj karatea, tjelohranitelj, „sve sam bio“, kaže. Ondje je upoznao ključne ljude koji su mu kasnije u životu puno pomogli, a i on je njima radio razne stvari i bio im trener.

U Rimu je bio tjelohranitelj **Carla Figlietta**, Talijana kojeg naziva „kraljem kave“. Napominje da to nije bio klasičan posao od 24 sata. Navečer su obilazili klubove, a danju je vodio školu karatea i učio jezike. Ljudi iz tog kruga pomogli su mu da ode u **London**. Ondje je živio u velikom stanu na **Prince of Wales Terrace**, a domaćini su ga vodili po londonskim klubovima. „Tako je sve to i počelo“, kaže.

Presudan poticaj došao je od **Irene Papas**, grčke glumice poznate po ulozi u „Medei“, koja je tada snimala veliki projekt sa Zaferellijem, kako ga gost spominje. Bili su dobri prijatelji. Lupino je s njom nekoliko puta putovao u Grčku i vozio je ondje. Nakon što je vidjela male sporedne uloge koje je imao u Italiji, rekla mu je da mora u New York, u školu **Stelle Adler**, jer ima talent. Lupino vjeruje da je to dobro procijenila, jer je poznavala i Branda. Glumica je umrla prije tri-četiri godine.

U Ameriku ipak nije mogao odmah, jer nije znao engleski. Do tada je, kaže, cijeli život samo trenirao:
- **hrvanje**
- **kajak na divljim vodama**
- **karate**, u kojem je bio „dosta veliki“ šampion

U Italiji je nastupao i za ekipu koja je postala momčadski prvak Italije. Sve je to, kaže, bila priprema za New York. Nakon dvije godine u Londonu, gdje je također radio s važnim ljudima, krenuo je „s dva kofera preko Atlantika“.

Lupino priznaje da tu priču više ne može pričati jer ima previše verzija i poveznica. Voditelj mu predlaže da napiše knjigu, a gost odgovara da bi trebale „dvije knjige“. Umjesto toga, o njemu se snima dokumentarni film, pa će se pojaviti i u Deborinu i u vlastitom filmu.
sections.subtitle_en: Rome, karate, and nights with the coffee king: the long road to America
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino recounts Roman days and meeting actress Irene Papas
sections.content_en:
To the question of how he ended up in America, Lupino replies that his first destination was **Rome**, where he spent four years. He was a karate teacher, a bodyguard, "I was everything," he says. There he met key people who later helped him a lot in life, and he also did various things for them and was their trainer.

In Rome he was the bodyguard of **Carlo Figlietto**, an Italian whom he calls the "coffee king". He notes that it was not a classic 24-hour job. In the evening they toured clubs, and during the day he ran a karate school and studied languages. People from that circle helped him go to **London**. There he lived in a large apartment on **Prince of Wales Terrace**, and the hosts took him around London clubs. "That's how it all started," he says.

The decisive encouragement came from **Irene Papas**, the Greek actress known for her role in "Medea", who was at that time shooting a major project with Zaferelli, as the guest mentions him. They were good friends. Lupino traveled with her several times to Greece and drove her there. After seeing the small supporting roles he had in Italy, she told him he had to go to New York, to **Stella Adler**'s school, because he had talent. Lupino believes she judged that well, because she also knew Brando. The actress died three or four years ago.

However, he could not go to America immediately, because he did not know English. Until then, he says, his whole life he only trained:
- **wrestling**
- **whitewater kayaking**
- **karate**, in which he was a "fairly big" champion

In Italy he also competed for a team that became the team champion of Italy. All of that, he says, was preparation for New York. After two years in London, where he also worked with important people, he set off "with two suitcases across the Atlantic".

Lupino admits that he can no longer tell that story because there are too many versions and connections. The host suggests that he write a book, and the guest replies that "two books" would be needed. Instead, a documentary film is being shot about him, so he will appear both in Deborah's film and in his own.

sections.subtitle: Studio 54 je već bio na izdisaju, a Lupino tek pred kamerom
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino objašnjava kako je postao model za Deborah Turbovel
sections.content:
Voditelj se pita o legendarnom **Studiju 54**. Lupino ga ispravlja: taj klub u njegovu životu nije igrao veliku ulogu. Kad je stigao u New York, krajem 1979. i 1980., klub je već bio pri kraju i definitivno se zatvorio oko 1980.–1981. Vrhunac je, prema njegovim riječima, bio 1977., 1978. i 1979. U New Yorku, objašnjava, nijedan klub ne traje dulje od pet godina.

Nakon toga došla je era u kojoj se probio, iako u to vrijeme još nije bio fotograf. Fotografom je postao zahvaljujući **Deborah Turbovel**. Ona mu je napravila casting, radio je za nju i dobro su se slagali. Kasnije je postao njezin **ekskluzivni model**.

Na pitanje što je u njemu prepoznala, Lupino odgovara da ju je privukao njegov **„Slavic look“**, odnosno slavenski izgled.
sections.subtitle_en: Studio 54 was already on its last legs, and Lupino only before the camera
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino explains how he became a model for Deborah Turbovel
sections.content_en:
The host wonders about the legendary **Studio 54**. Lupino corrects him: that club did not play a big role in his life. When he arrived in New York, in late 1979 and 1980, the club was already nearing its end and definitely closed around 1980–1981. The peak, according to his words, was 1977, 1978, and 1979. In New York, he explains, no club lasts longer than five years.

After that came the era in which he broke through, although at that time he was not yet a photographer. He became a photographer thanks to **Deborah Turbovel**. She held a casting for him, he worked for her, and they got along well. Later he became her **exclusive model**.

When asked what she recognized in him, Lupino replies that she was attracted by his **"Slavic look"**, that is, Slavic appearance.

sections.subtitle: Jet set nekad i danas: 90 posto prijatelja više nije živo
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino govori o prijateljima iz newyorškog jet seta koji su preminuli
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da je Lupino bio dio tadašnjeg **jet seta**. Gost to potvrđuje, ali naglašava da ga slava nikad nije zavela. Većina ljudi, kaže, kad ih slava uhvati, „odu na kvasinu“. Njemu je ona bila samo stepenica prema daljnjem razvoju.

Na pitanje kakva je bila tadašnja elita izbliza, bez kamera, Lupino odgovara da su ljudi nekada bili originalniji. Današnji su, smatra, učili od njih i sve je postalo „copy-paste“. Posebno mu smetaju **crveni tepisi**: ljudi bi, kaže, sve dali samo da ih se vidi i da skupe lajkove. Odijela se šivaju posebno za jedno pojavljivanje, što mu je nepojmljivo. Voditelj to sažima riječju „praznina“, a Lupino dodaje da se pita gdje je tu kvaliteta. Izdvojiti može tek nekolicinu ljudi, većinom glumaca koje je uvijek volio, i to „na prste jedne ruke“.

Na pitanje s kim je bio posebno blizak, iznosi poražavajući podatak: oko **90 posto** ljudi koje je poznavao više nije živo. Živjeli su preintenzivno, drogirali se i alkoholizirali. U New Yorku danas ima tek nekoliko ljudi iz tog doba s kojima je u kontaktu. Kad ga vide, ne vjeruju kako izgleda i šale se da se „napravio kao mumija“. Voditelj dodaje da su mnogi od njih sebi dodali i botoksa, a Lupino priznaje da se, kad ih danas vidi, pita kako je prošlo tih 30 godina.
sections.subtitle_en: Jet set then and now: 90 percent of friends are no longer alive
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino speaks about friends from the New York jet set who passed away
sections.content_en:
The host reminds that Lupino was part of the **jet set** at the time. The guest confirms this, but emphasizes that fame never seduced him. Most people, he says, when fame catches them, "go sour". For him, it was only a stepping stone toward further development.

When asked what the elite of that time was like up close, without cameras, Lupino replies that people in the past were more original. Today's, he believes, learned from them and everything has become "copy-paste". He is especially bothered by **red carpets**: people, he says, would give anything just to be seen and collect likes. Suits are tailored specifically for a single appearance, which is inconceivable to him. The host summarizes this with the word "emptiness", and Lupino adds that he wonders where the quality is in that. He can single out only a handful of people, mostly actors he always loved, and that "on the fingers of one hand".

When asked with whom he was particularly close, he brings out a devastating fact: about **90 percent** of the people he knew are no longer alive. They lived too intensely, did drugs, and abused alcohol. In New York today he has only a few people from that era with whom he is in touch. When they see him, they do not believe what he looks like and joke that he "made himself like a mummy". The host adds that many of them also added Botox to themselves, and Lupino admits that when he sees them today, he wonders how those 30 years passed.

sections.subtitle: Manekenke su nekad bile bogovi, danas su tu botoks i AI filteri
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino uspoređuje nekadašnje i današnje manekenke i modu
sections.content:
Voditelj ga naziva majstorom erotske fotografije, a Lupino skromno odbija i tu titulu i „velemajstora“. Erotsku fotografiju vidi kao još jednu stepenicu prema onome što je danas. Njegova prva djela, prenosi riječi jednog kritičara, već su imala „sculptural look“. Muškarci i žene na njegovim fotografijama izgledali su kao skulpture.

Na usporedbu današnjih i nekadašnjih manekenki odgovara jasno: manekenke su nekada bile **kao bogovi**. Danas, kaže, nema ni prave mode. Nestalo je dizajnera koji su bili ikone, poput **Galliana** i **Karla Lagerfelda**. Zlatno doba mode smješta u 70-e, 80-e i dijelom 90-e godine.

Voditelj primjećuje da su žene nekada bile prirodnije, a Lupino se nadovezuje kritikom botoksa, a zatim i fotografija koje se dodatno uljepšavaju umjetnom inteligencijom. Ljudi mu, kaže, šalju takve slike i ponosni su što izgledaju drugačije. Kad ih uživo vidi, pomisli: pa to nisi ti. Voditelj se pita odakle potreba da se netko prikaže jednim licem, a pred sugovornikom se pojavi kao posve druga osoba.
sections.subtitle_en: Models used to be gods, today there are Botox and AI filters
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino compares past and present models and fashion
sections.content_en:
The host calls him a master of erotic photography, and Lupino modestly rejects both that title and "grandmaster". He sees erotic photography as another stepping stone toward what he is today. His first works, he conveys the words of a critic, already had a "sculptural look". The men and women in his photographs looked like sculptures.

To the comparison of today's and past models he responds clearly: models used to be **like gods**. Today, he says, there is not even real fashion. Designers who were icons, like **Galliano** and **Karl Lagerfeld**, have disappeared. He places the golden age of fashion in the 70s, 80s, and partly 90s.

The host observes that women used to be more natural, and Lupino follows up with criticism of Botox, and then of photographs that are additionally beautified with artificial intelligence. People, he says, send him such pictures and are proud to look different. When he sees them in person, he thinks: but that's not you. The host wonders where the need comes from for someone to present themselves with one face, and appear before an interlocutor as a completely different person.

sections.subtitle: Oštra kritika ultrabogataša: Afrika gladuje, a oni žele na Mars
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino kritizira bogataše koji ne pomažu gladnima
sections.content:
Na pitanje gdje je pošlo po krivu, Lupino odgovara da je cijeli svijet krenuo krivim putem. Ističe koliko je ratova i gladi u svijetu, a koliko istodobno ima novih **ultrabogataša**.

Jedan od njih bi, tvrdi gost, mogao sam nahraniti cijelu **Afriku** nekoliko godina, ali nitko to ne čini, jer svi koji imaju novac samo žele još više. Izgubili su, kako se slaže s voditeljem, dodir sa stvarnošću. Najgore mu je to što se smatraju bogovima. Voditelj dodaje da su se počeli igrati ljudskim sudbinama.

Lupinu smeta i to što ljudi to toleriraju i takve osobe veličaju kao talentirane. Pritom se, kaže, „pokraju“ **Teslu**, bez kojega ne bi bilo ničega. Ironizira i planove o odlasku na **Mars**: ne može se živjeti ni na Mjesecu, a oni bi na Mars, samo da ih ljudi gledaju kao bogove.
sections.subtitle_en: Sharp criticism of the ultra-rich: Africa is starving, and they want to go to Mars
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino criticizes the wealthy who do not help the starving
sections.content_en:
To the question of where things went wrong, Lupino replies that the whole world took the wrong path. He highlights how many wars and famine there are in the world, and how many new **ultra-wealthy** people there are at the same time.

One of them, the guest claims, could single-handedly feed all of **Africa** for several years, but no one does it, because everyone who has money just wants even more. They have lost, as he agrees with the host, touch with reality. What is worst to him is that they consider themselves gods. The host adds that they have started playing with human destinies.

Lupino is also bothered by people tolerating this and glorifying such people as talented. In doing so, he says, they "steal" from **Tesla**, without whom there would be nothing. He also ironizes plans about going to **Mars**: one cannot even live on the Moon, and they would like to go to Mars, just so people look at them as gods.

sections.subtitle: Kad su svi fotografi: mobiteli, influencerice i „nova žena“
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino govori o tome kako su mobiteli svakoga pretvorili u fotografa
sections.content:
Razgovor se vraća fotografiji i pojavi mobitela. Danas su, kako kaže voditelj, svi fotografi. Lupinu je to drago, ali ga ponekad gnjave molbama da ih „poslika mobitelom“. On danas fotografira samo ono što želi i koga želi. Obavezno snima **bolesnu djecu za humanitarne akcije**, a uz to se prihvaća samo nečeg posebnog. Sitne poslove više ne radi.

Voditelj napominje da mobitel nije uništio fotografiju, nego ju je popularizirao, ali se danas fotografira svašta. Lupino smatra da upravo zato njegove fotografije danas imaju još veću vrijednost, jer su drugačije. Ljudi ga uglavnom pamte po **crno-bijelim fotografijama**, ali podsjeća da je radio i posebne fotografije u boji.

Voditelj se pita gubi li ženska ljepota na vrijednosti kad je sve dostupno i svatko sam sebe fotografira. Lupino primjećuje mnoštvo influencerica koje se fotografiraju sto puta na dan. Na pitanje što se dogodilo ženama, odgovara da su za to možda krivi muškarci. Vrijeme je donijelo promjenu u kojoj su žene, prema njegovu mišljenju, izgubile nešto od onoga što su nekada imale. Taj fenomen naziva **„new women“**, pa i **„new race“**.
sections.subtitle_en: When everyone is a photographer: mobile phones, female influencers, and the "new woman"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino speaks about how mobile phones turned everyone into a photographer
sections.content_en:
The conversation returns to photography and the emergence of mobile phones. Today, as the host says, everyone is a photographer. Lupino is glad about that, but people sometimes bother him with requests to "snap them with a phone". Today he photographs only what he wants and whom he wants. He without fail photographs **sick children for humanitarian drives**, and besides that takes on only something special. He no longer does minor jobs.

The host notes that the mobile phone did not destroy photography, but popularized it, but today anything and everything gets photographed. Lupino considers that precisely because of this his photographs have even greater value today, because they are different. People mainly remember him for **black-and-white photographs**, but he reminds that he also did special color photographs.

The host wonders whether female beauty loses value when everything is accessible and everyone takes photos of themselves. Lupino observes a multitude of female influencers who photograph themselves a hundred times a day. To the question of what happened to women, he replies that men might be to blame for that. Time has brought a change in which women, in his opinion, have lost something of what they once had. He calls that phenomenon **"new women"**, even **"new race"**.

sections.subtitle: Lupinizam: stil koji se nigdje ne može svrstati
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino objašnjava pojam lupinizma i kritizira kopiranje u fotografiji
sections.content:
Voditelj prelazi na Lupinovo današnje glavno zanimanje, **skulpture** i vlastiti stil nazvan **lupinizam**. Gost objašnjava da je taj pristup postojao već u fotografiji. Upravo zbog njega cijeli ga je svijet znao već šest mjeseci nakon što je počeo raditi, a svi su ga objavljivali jer je imao **„different look“**.

U početku su mnogi mislili da će kopirati Deborah Turbovel, ali njihove su fotografije, kaže, „kao nebo i zemlja“. Međusobno su se poštovali, a njezin ga je rad inspirirao. Žali što se suvremena fotografija samo ponavlja: od 80-ih se, smatra, nije napravilo ništa novo. Mnogi danas rade „hommage“ fotografiji iz 70-ih i 80-ih, kad su nastajale najbolje fotografije. Kao uzore koje se oponaša spominje **Helmuta Newtona**. Većina portreta žena, prema njegovu mišljenju, ne razlikuje se od već viđenog, samo je „na drugi način začinjena“.

Na pitanje može li se lupinizam smatrati zasebnim umjetničkim pravcem, Lupino kaže da taj naziv nije sam smislio. Ljudi ga, kaže, ne mogu nigdje svrstati. Vjeruje da će se to tek osjetiti za desetak ili dvadesetak godina, kad se „sve prokuha“. Već mu neki govore da će se za dvadeset ili trideset godina njegov stil učiti na akademijama. Kad ga voditelj pita spaja li tim stilom fotografiju i kiparstvo, odgovara da spaja **život**. Umjetnost ima mnogo razina, a ljudi većinom gledaju samo jednu.

Priznaje da možda zvuči bahato, ali zbog općeg kopiranja više ne želi komercijalno fotografirati. To bi za njega bilo kao „bacanje bisera pred svinje“. Voditelj zaključuje da je postao avangarda jer se nije bojao riskirati. Lupino se slaže i prepričava iskustvo sa seminara: studenti su ga umjesto o tome kako radi pitali koliko se to plaća. „I onda izgubiš volju“, kaže.
sections.subtitle_en: Lupinism: a style that cannot be classified anywhere
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino explains the concept of Lupinism and criticizes copying in photography
sections.content_en:
The host moves on to Lupino's main occupation today, **sculptures** and his own style called **Lupinism**. The guest explains that this approach already existed in photography. Precisely because of it, the whole world knew him already six months after he started working, and everyone published him because he had a **"different look"**.

In the beginning, many thought he would copy Deborah Turbovel, but their photographs, he says, are "like night and day". They respected each other, and her work inspired him. He regrets that contemporary photography only repeats itself: since the 80s, he considers, nothing new has been made. Many today do an "hommage" to photography from the 70s and 80s, when the best photographs were being created. As role models that are imitated he mentions **Helmut Newton**. Most portraits of women, in his opinion, do not differ from what has already been seen, only "seasoned in a different way".

When asked whether Lupinism can be considered a separate artistic movement, Lupino says that he did not come up with that name himself. People, he says, cannot classify him anywhere. He believes that this will only be felt in ten or twenty years, when "everything simmers down". Some are already telling him that in twenty or thirty years his style will be taught at academies. When the host asks him whether he combines photography and sculpture with that style, he replies that he combines **life**. Art has many levels, and people mostly look at only one.

He admits that he might sound arrogant, but due to general copying he no longer wants to do commercial photography. For him that would be like "casting pearls before swine". The host concludes that he became avant-garde because he was not afraid to take risks. Lupino agrees and recounts an experience from a seminar: students asked him how much it pays instead of how he works. "And then you lose the will," he says.

sections.subtitle: Lajkovi, lažni profili i prevarant koji je tražio 300 eura u Lupinovo ime
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino prepričava slučaj prevaranta koji se lažno predstavljao njegovim imenom
sections.content:
„Bože moj, lajkove. Tko je to smislio?“, pita se Lupino. Voditelj spominje dokumentarac **„The Social Dilemma“**, u kojem čovjek koji je osmislio lajkove kaže da ih je zamislio kao nešto pozitivno što će ljude usrećiti. Kad je, međutim, čuo da se prvi čovjek ubio, dao je otkaz u **Silicijskoj dolini**. Lupino se nadovezuje da i djeca stradavaju zbog interneta. Iako je internet neophodan za posao, smatra da je sve pretjerano i da „mora negdje puknuti“. Isto predviđa i za umjetnu inteligenciju, koja bi mogla donijeti zlo.

Gost se suočio i s mračnom stranom mreža. U jednom je trenutku postojalo i po **deset lažnih profila** s njegovim imenom. Zato je odlučio imati jedan službeni profil i ne objavljivati svaki dan, ali ga održavati, jer bi se inače „netko ugurao unutra“.

Iznosi i konkretan slučaj. Javio mu se otac jedne djevojke i pitao zašto ga Lupino nije nazvao izravno. Netko se predstavio kao Lupino i od djevojke tražio **300 eura** predujma za fotografiranje. Voditelj spominje i lažne reklame u kojima se poznate osobe navodno preporučuju kreme, a protiv kojih je pravno vrlo teško djelovati. Lupino se našali da je bilo i „Lupino kolača“. Dvije do tri godine trebalo mu je da se riješi starih lažnih profila.
sections.subtitle_en: Likes, fake profiles, and a fraudster who demanded 300 euros in Lupino's name
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino recounts the case of a fraudster who falsely impersonated him by name
sections.content_en:
"My God, likes. Who came up with that?", wonders Lupino. The host mentions the documentary **"The Social Dilemma"**, in which the man who devised likes says he envisioned them as something positive that would make people happy. When, however, he heard that the first man committed suicide, he quit his job in **Silicon Valley**. Lupino follows up that children are also harmed because of the internet. Although the internet is indispensable for work, he considers that everything is exaggerated and that "it has to burst somewhere". He predicts the same for artificial intelligence, which could bring evil.

The guest also faced the dark side of social networks. At one point there were even **ten fake profiles** with his name. That is why he decided to have one official profile and not post every day, but maintain it, because otherwise "someone would squeeze in".

He also presents a specific case. The father of a young woman contacted him and asked why Lupino had not called him directly. Someone introduced himself as Lupino and demanded from the young woman a **300-euro** advance for a photoshoot. The host also mentions fake advertisements in which famous people allegedly recommend creams, against which it is legally very difficult to act. Lupino jokes that there were even "Lupino cakes". It took him two to three years to get rid of old fake profiles.

sections.subtitle: AI tek usputno: suradnja s Brendanom i recenzija s Oxforda
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino govori o suradniku Brendanu i recenziji Andrewa Hemingwaya
sections.content:
Na pitanje koliko koristi umjetnu inteligenciju u poslu, Lupino kaže da vrlo malo. Ipak, surađuje s Englezom **Brendanom**, kojemu je povjerio dio posla jer mu je pouzdan. Brendan piše eseje i novelu koja će biti ilustrirana Lupinovim slikama, a već mu je napisao i neke tekstove.

Brendan mu je pronašao i **Andrewa Hemingwaya**, profesora umjetnosti s **Oxforda**, koji je pogledao Lupinove radove i napisao recenziju. Gost Brendana opisuje kao vrlo pametnog čovjeka koji je prepoznao njegov „touch“, njegov osobni dodir.

Brendan pomaže i oko dokumentarnog filma o Lupinu. Na njemu ekipa radi već **sedam godina** i, kaže gost, film je pri kraju. Brendanu se obraća i kad djelu treba dati ime. To nije lako, jer Lupino ima već oko **1500 radova**.
sections.subtitle_en: AI only incidentally: collaboration with Brendan and a review from Oxford
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino speaks about collaborator Brendan and Andrew Hemingway's review
sections.content_en:
When asked how much he uses artificial intelligence in his work, Lupino says very little. Still, he collaborates with the Englishman **Brendan**, to whom he entrusted part of the work because he is reliable to him. Brendan writes essays and a novella that will be illustrated with Lupino's paintings, and has already written some texts for him.

Brendan also found for him **Andrew Hemingway**, an art professor from **Oxford**, who looked at Lupino's works and wrote a review. The guest describes Brendan as a very smart man who recognized his "touch", his personal touch.

Brendan also helps around the documentary film about Lupino. The crew has been working on it for **seven years** already and, the guest says, the film is nearing completion. He also turns to Brendan when a work needs to be given a name. That is not easy, because Lupino already has around **1,500 works**.

sections.subtitle: Izložba lupinizma? Najmanje dva kamiona
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino opisuje svoje monumentalne skulpture i izložbe
sections.content:
Lupino ističe da najviše voli **velike skulpture**. Ako netko želi izložbu lupinizma, kaže, potreban je jedan ili dva kamiona. Manje postave ne smatra pravim izložbama. Riječ je uglavnom o humanitarnim akcijama u kojima izloži slike, proda ih, a novac ide djeci. Velike je stvari, priznaje, vrlo teško izložiti.

Njegovi su radovi nedavno bili izloženi na **Špancirfestu**, a trenutno pregovara o postavu u jednom **dvorcu u Zagorju**. Voditelj primjećuje da u radu ima i mnogo religijskih motiva. Lupino potvrđuje i naglašava da je riječ o djelima višim od tri, pa i četiri metra.

Na pitanje je li mu religija važna, odgovara da jest i da je uvijek bio „u tome“, ali ne fanatično. Život bez vjere, smatra, nije potpun, jer novac čovjeka neće spasiti.
sections.subtitle_en: An exhibition of Lupinism? At least two trucks
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino describes his monumental sculptures and exhibitions
sections.content_en:
Lupino emphasizes that he likes **large sculptures** the most. If someone wants an exhibition of Lupinism, he says, one or two trucks are needed. He does not consider smaller setups real exhibitions. Those are mainly humanitarian drives where he exhibits paintings, sells them, and the money goes to children. Big things, he admits, are very difficult to exhibit.

His works were recently exhibited at **Špancirfest**, and he is currently negotiating an installation in a **castle in Zagorje**. The host notices that there are also many religious motifs in his work. Lupino confirms and emphasizes that these are works taller than three, even four meters.

When asked whether religion is important to him, he replies that it is and that he was always "in it", but not fanatically. Life without faith, he considers, is not complete, because money will not save a person.

sections.subtitle: Influencer prije influencera: ludilo downtown New Yorka 80-ih
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino prepričava anegdotu iz newyorških klubova 80-ih
sections.content:
Na pitanje s kim mu je bilo najteže surađivati, Lupino odgovara da je uglavnom radio s ljudima koji su znali što radi i bili spremni na to. Prisjeća se jedne anegdote iz newyorških klubova. U klub je jednom izašao s bivšom suprugom argentinskog veleposlanika i nosio ju je na ramenu. „Valjda mi je oprostio“, kaže kroz smijeh.

To je razdoblje opisuje kao **ludilo**: biti u downtownu među prvih deset, kako kaže, „kao influencer“ 80-ih nije bilo lako. Voditelj napominje da se tada to još nije zvalo tako.

O današnjim influencerima Lupino isprva samo uzdiše, a zatim ih brani usporedbom s **Andyjem Warholom**, koji je rekao da će svatko biti slavan pet minuta. Priznaje da ni njima nije lako i da je prije više kritizirao. Danas se drži pravila da, ako ne može pohvaliti, neće ni kritizirati.
sections.subtitle_en: An influencer before influencers: madness of downtown New York in the 80s
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino recounts an anecdote from New York clubs in the 80s
sections.content_en:
When asked with whom it was most difficult for him to collaborate, Lupino replies that he mostly worked with people who knew what he did and were ready for it. He recalls an anecdote from New York clubs. He once went out to a club with the ex-wife of the Argentine ambassador and carried her on his shoulder. "I guess he forgave me," he says through laughter.

He describes that period as **madness**: being downtown among the top ten, as he says, "like an influencer" in the 80s was not easy. The host notes that back then it was not yet called that.

About today's influencers Lupino at first only sighs, and then defends them by comparison with **Andy Warhol**, who said that everyone will be famous for five minutes. He admits that it is not easy for them either and that earlier he criticized more. Today he adheres to the rule that if he cannot praise, he will not criticize either.

sections.subtitle: Hrvati žive tuđe živote: od drugog kata do skupih automobila
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino govori o hrvatskom mentalitetu i zavisti
sections.content:
Govoreći o influencerima, Lupino se dotiče i hrvatskog mentaliteta. Smatra da su Hrvati skloni **živjeti tuđe živote**, dok vani svatko ide svojim putem. Kod nas je, kaže, važno što ima drugi: ako on ima, moram i ja. Voditelj se nadovezuje poznatom šalom o susjedovoj kući koja je malo viša, pa se sljedeće ljeto zida drugi kat.

Lupino prepričava kako ga je **Brendan** pitao zašto na hrvatskim cestama ima toliko skupih automobila, kojih nema ni drugdje. „To ti je Hrvatska“, odgovorio mu je. Ljudi se, smatra, vežu za stvari umjesto da se okrenu nečemu što ima sadržaj.

Voditelj zamišlja kritičare koji bi rekli da je njemu lako govoriti. Lupino podsjeća kako je počeo: s **dva kofera u New York**, sa 24 ili 25 godina. Nije bilo lako, kaže, ali vodio ga je entuzijazam i misao „idem, idem“.
sections.subtitle_en: Croats live other people's lives: from the second floor to expensive cars
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino speaks about the Croatian mentality and envy
sections.content_en:
Speaking about influencers, Lupino also touches upon the Croatian mentality. He considers that Croats are prone to **living other people's lives**, while abroad everyone goes their own way. In our parts, he says, what another has is important: if he has it, I must too. The host follows up with a well-known joke about the neighbor's house being slightly taller, so next summer a second floor gets built.

Lupino recounts how **Brendan** asked him why there are so many expensive cars on Croatian roads, which do not exist elsewhere either. "That's Croatia for you," he answered him. People, he believes, get attached to things instead of turning to something that has substance.

The host imagines critics who would say that it is easy for him to talk. Lupino reminds how he started: with **two suitcases to New York**, at 24 or 25 years old. It was not easy, he says, but enthusiasm and the thought "I'm going, I'm going" drove him.

sections.subtitle: Povratak zbog rata i Hrvatska kakvu nitko nije zamišljao
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino objašnjava zašto se vratio u Hrvatsku početkom rata
sections.content:
U Hrvatsku se odlučio vratiti kad je počeo rat. Gledajući **Vukovar** i ljude koji bježe van, nije mogao ostati, nego je osjetio da mora biti ovdje.

Na pitanje je li Hrvatsku zamišljao ovakvom kakva je danas, odgovara da nitko nije. Smatra da će još dugo trebati da kod nas zaživi zapadni mentalitet. Glavnu grešku ponovno vidi u tome što Hrvati žive tuđe živote. Svi su, kaže, „genetski“ skloni ljubomori, iako za sebe tvrdi da nije takav. Kritizira i sklonost grupiranju u udruge kako bi se „više čapilo“ i profitiralo. Nedostaje mu iskrenosti i rada „sa srcem“, umjesto pravila „koga znaš“ i „imaš li tamo koga“.

Voditelj se šali da ćemo pokvariti i Europsku uniju. Lupino smatra da smo se riješili mnogo toga, ali da sada treba doći **prosperitet**. Ako to ne napravimo, upozorava, „ne piše nam se dobro“. Demografija pada, a stranci se, govoreći općenito, kod nas ne vole. To, kaže, nije dobro za mladu zemlju koja želi napredovati.
sections.subtitle_en: Return because of the war and a Croatia no one imagined
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino explains why he returned to Croatia at the beginning of the war
sections.content_en:
He decided to return to Croatia when the war started. Watching **Vukovar** and people fleeing abroad, he could not stay, but felt that he had to be here.

To the question of whether he imagined Croatia like this as it is today, he replies that no one did. He considers that it will take a long time for a Western mentality to take root among us. He sees the main mistake again in the fact that Croats live other people's lives. Everyone is, he says, "genetically" prone to jealousy, although he claims for himself that he is not like that. He also criticizes the tendency of grouping into associations in order to "grab more" and profit. He misses honesty and working "with heart", instead of the rules "whom you know" and "do you have someone there".

The host jokes that we will corrupt the European Union as well. Lupino considers that we got rid of many things, but that now **prosperity** should come. If we don't do that, he warns, "things do not look good for us". Demographics are declining, and foreigners, speaking generally, are not liked among us. That, he says, is not good for a young country that wants to progress.

sections.subtitle: Talenta ima, ali ga drže uhljebi: sport koji nestaje
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino govori o neiskorištenim mladim talentima i propadanju sporta
sections.content:
Voditelj kao primjer vrijednog mladog čovjeka navodi **Galeba**, 23-godišnjaka koji radi od jutra do mraka. Lupino ističe da Hrvatska ima mnogo talenta, ali da je neiskorišten i bez prilike, jer „uhljebi drže sve“. Voditelj se pita žele li mladi prebrzo do svega. Lupino se slaže da tu nedostaje strpljenja, a internet je to dodatno ubrzao.

Posebno se dotiče **sporta**, kojim se i sam cijeli život bavio. Sportaše bi trebalo više cijeniti, a kod nas se financiraju samo nogomet i još nekoliko sportova. Voditelj dodaje da to posebno pogađa individualne sportove. Lupino upozorava da gubimo ono po čemu smo bili poznati u svijetu: košarke, kaže, više nema kao nekada, a ni rukometa kakav je bio. Kritizira i hrvatsku samodopadnost u stilu „mi smo najbolji“.

Nogomet opisuje kao „veliku kuhinju“, a voditelj dodaje da su talenti na zadnjem mjestu jer se zarada traži odmah. Lupino smatra da domaći menadžeri nemaju **etiku** kakva postoji vani, gdje je menadžer „bog“ koji pronalazi talente. Zaključuje da bi sport trebao biti klupski i zajednički, a ne usmjeren na nekoliko zvijezda.
sections.subtitle_en: There is talent, but party hacks hold it: sports that are disappearing
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino speaks about unutilized young talents and the decline of sports
sections.content_en:
The host cites as an example of a hardworking young man **Galeb**, a 23-year-old who works from dawn till dusk. Lupino emphasizes that Croatia has a lot of talent, but that it is unutilized and without opportunity, because "party hacks hold everything". The host wonders whether young people want to reach everything too quickly. Lupino agrees that patience is lacking there, and the internet has further accelerated that.

He specifically touches upon **sports**, which he himself engaged in all his life. Athletes should be appreciated more, and in our country only soccer and a few other sports are funded. The host adds that this particularly affects individual sports. Lupino warns that we are losing what we were known for in the world: basketball, he says, is no longer what it used to be, nor handball as it once was. He also criticizes Croatian complacency in the style of "we are the best".

He describes soccer as a "big kitchen", and the host adds that talents are in last place because earnings are sought immediately. Lupino considers that domestic managers do not have the **ethics** that exist abroad, where a manager is "god" who finds talents. He concludes that sports should be club-based and collective, and not directed toward a few stars.

sections.subtitle: Umjetnost ne čeka narudžbu, a fotografi su propali
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino govori o umjetnicima koji rade samo po narudžbi
sections.content:
Slično kao u sportu, Lupino vidi problem i u vlastitoj struci. Mnogi domaći umjetnici, kaže, ne počinju raditi dok ne dobiju **narudžbu**. Umjetnik, smatra, mora stalno stvarati, i to tako da netko uzme njegovo djelo, a ne da ga naruči. Kad mu netko želi naručiti bistu, odgovara da je neće raditi po želji. Možda se naručitelj na kraju neće ni prepoznati, ali djelo će biti vrijednije. Umjetnost, ističe, nema narudžbu. Narudžba dolazi sama kad netko postane umjetnik.

Kod nas, nastavlja, umjetnici čekaju da im netko, primjerice crkva, naruči oltar, umjesto da sami stvaraju. Ipak, dijelom ih razumije. On je financijski „potkovan“ iz drugih izvora pa si to može priuštiti, dok drugi to ne mogu i zato češće pristaju na kompromise.

Voditelj podsjeća da se od fotografije nekada moglo dobro zaraditi. Lupino kaže da danas, zbog mobitela, gotovo ništa. Žao mu je mnogih kolega fotografa za koje kaže da su „malo propali“. Na pitanje je li sam razvijao fotografije, potvrđuje da je nekada jest.
sections.subtitle_en: Art does not wait for a commission, and photographers have gone ruined
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino speaks about artists who work only on commission
sections.content_en:
Similarly as in sports, Lupino sees a problem in his own profession as well. Many domestic artists, he says, do not start working until they get a **commission**. An artist, he considers, must create constantly, and in such a way that someone takes his work, not that they commission it. When someone wants to commission a bust from him, he replies that he will not make it according to their wishes. The client might not even recognize themselves in the end, but the work will be more valuable. Art, he emphasizes, has no commission. The commission comes by itself when someone becomes an artist.

In our country, he continues, artists wait for someone, for example the church, to commission an altar from them, instead of creating themselves. Still, he partly understands them. He is financially "well-heeled" from other sources so he can afford it, while others cannot and therefore more often agree to compromises.

The host reminds that one could once earn good money from photography. Lupino says that today, because of mobile phones, almost nothing. He feels sorry for many photographer colleagues about whom he says that they have "gone a bit ruined". When asked whether he developed photographs himself, he confirms that he once did.

sections.subtitle: Najteži je bio emocionalni napor, a najviše su ga dirnula djeca
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino se prisjeća trenutka kad se rasplakao pred djecom kojima je pomogao
sections.content:
Fotografija je za Lupina bila **mukotrpna**, ali ne fizički, jer je cijeli život u formi. Iscrpljivala ga je emocionalno, jer je u svaku fotografiju morao uložiti vlastite emocije. Voditelj napominje da se to vidjelo na fotografijama. Gost ističe da je posebno teško bilo fotografirati za **humanitarne akcije**.

Voditelj ga podsjeća na trenutak kad se rasplakao. Lupino opisuje susret s djecom za koju je radio i kojima je nešto poklonio. Kad ih je vidio, zahvalna, nije mogao zadržati suze. „Teško je to“, kaže. Voditelj dodaje da je dječja zahvalnost iskrena jer djeca ne znaju lagati.
sections.subtitle_en: The hardest was the emotional effort, and children touched him the most
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino recalls the moment when he burst into tears in front of children he helped
sections.content_en:
Photography was **painstaking** for Lupino, but not physically, because he has been in shape all his life. It exhausted him emotionally, because he had to invest his own emotions into every photograph. The host notes that this was visible in the photographs. The guest points out that it was particularly difficult to photograph for **humanitarian drives**.

The host reminds him of the moment when he burst into tears. Lupino describes an encounter with children for whom he worked and to whom he gifted something. When he saw them, grateful, he could not hold back tears. "It is hard," he says. The host adds that children's gratitude is sincere because children do not know how to lie.

sections.subtitle: Radionica u Varaždinu i najljepše žene na svijetu
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino kroz smijeh odgovara da su najljepše žene susjede
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da je Lupino, kad god su se čuli, uvijek nešto brusio ili lupao u svojoj radionici u **Varaždinu**. Gost potvrđuje da bez rada ne može i da stajanja nema dok god se može. Pritom citira talijansku izreku o tome da se živi dok se živi.

Na pitanje koje su po njemu najljepše žene na svijetu, odgovara kratko: **susjede**. Susjeda je, kaže, uvijek najljepša, a voditelj dodaje: pogotovo kad dođe po šećer. Ozbiljnije, Lupino spominje dive iz prošlih vremena poput **Brigitte Bardot**, čije je doba prošlo. Za današnje „modaksirane“ ljepotice s mnogo lajkova kaže da ih ne gleda, iako priznaje da imaju veliko tržište jer se sviđaju mnogim muškarcima.
sections.subtitle_en: A workshop in Varaždin and the most beautiful women in the world
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino through laughter replies that the neighbor women are the most beautiful women
sections.content_en:
The host observes that Lupino, whenever they spoke, was always grinding or pounding something in his workshop in **Varaždin**. The guest confirms that he cannot live without work and that there is no stopping as long as one can. In doing so he cites an Italian saying about living while one is alive.

When asked who in his opinion are the most beautiful women in the world, he replies briefly: **the neighbor women**. A female neighbor, he says, is always the most beautiful, and the host adds: especially when she comes to borrow sugar. More seriously, Lupino mentions divas of past times like **Brigitte Bardot**, whose era has passed. Regarding today's "botoxed" beauties with many likes, he says that he does not look at them, although he admits that they have a big market because many men like them.

sections.subtitle: Pariz, dokumentarac i zimski bijeg na Tajland
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino govori o aktualnim projektima i godišnjem putovanju na Tajland
sections.content:
Govoreći o aktualnim projektima, Lupino ističe da će zbog filma o **Deborah Turbovel** najvjerojatnije još jednom morati u **Pariz**. Ekipa trenutno snima u **New Yorku**. Istodobno se intenzivno radi i na njegovu vlastitom dokumentarcu.

U siječnju putuje na **Tajland**, kamo odlazi svake godine kako bi se, kako kaže, napunio toplinom i inspiracijom. Voditelj se šali sa „susjedama“, a Lupino naglašava da ne ide onamo zbog žena, kao mnogi, niti u resorte. Odlazi u kraj oko **Bang Taoa**, koji smatra najljepšim.

Voli tamošnje ljude i njihovu **etiku**. Kao primjer navodi pušenje: ako netko sjedne pokraj tebe u restoranu i ti zapališ, on će uzeti stolicu i pomaknuti se, bez prigovaranja. Voditelj se prisjeća da smo se i mi nekada više smijali i pozdravljali, ali da nas je preuzeo newyorški tempo u kojem „samo pičimo“.
sections.subtitle_en: Paris, documentary, and a winter escape to Thailand
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino speaks about current projects and the annual trip to Thailand
sections.content_en:
Speaking about current projects, Lupino points out that because of the film about **Deborah Turbovel** he will most likely have to go to **Paris** one more time. The crew is currently filming in **New York**. At the same time, intensive work is also being done on his own documentary.

In January he travels to **Thailand**, where he goes every year in order to, as he says, recharge with warmth and inspiration. The host jokes about "female neighbors", and Lupino emphasizes that he does not go there because of women, like many, nor to resorts. He goes to the area around **Bang Tao**, which he considers the most beautiful.

He loves the people there and their **ethics**. As an example he cites smoking: if someone sits down next to you in a restaurant and you light up, they will take their chair and move away, without complaining. The host recalls that we also used to smile and greet each other more, but that the New York tempo took us over, in which we "just rush along".

sections.subtitle: Puni kafići, izgubljena tradicija i „event“ umjesto događaja
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino komentira pune kafiće i gubitak tradicije
sections.content:
Lupino uspoređuje Tajlanđane, koji su stalno zauzeti, s Hrvatima, kod kojih su **kafići uvijek puni**. Ne zna o čemu ljudi ondje razgovaraju, a voditelj sumnja da uglavnom samo skrolaju. Gost kaže da on nikad nije sjedio po kafićima jer za to nema vremena. Voditelj se šali da će to ipak učiniti nakon snimanja.

Voditelj otvara temu prebrzog odricanja od **tradicije i identiteta**. Ističe da Hrvatska pripada Europi, ali da ni ondje nije sve zlatno. Lupino suho odgovara da je „bolje nego Rusi“. Voditelj se prisjeća kako je s 25 godina baku smatrao zastarjelom, a danas shvaća da je ona samo pokušavala sačuvati nešto što se gubilo.

Lupino ističe da mu je Hrvatska, što se tiče same zemlje, „naj, naj, naj“. Ljeti ne ide nikamo jer mu je ljeto **Jadransko more i Dalmacija**. Zimi mu more nedostaje, pa tada putuje u toplije krajeve.

Voditelj se zatim osvrće na **anglizme** među mladima, primjerice „event“ umjesto „događaj“. Lupino to pripisuje internetskom rječniku i priznaje da ne zna kamo to vodi i kako će završiti, posebno s umjetnom inteligencijom.
sections.subtitle_en: Full cafes, lost tradition, and "event" instead of gathering
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino comments on full cafes and the loss of tradition
sections.content_en:
Lupino compares Thais, who are constantly busy, with Croats, among whom **cafes are always full**. He does not know what people talk about there, and the host suspects that they mostly just scroll. The guest says that he never sat around in cafes because he does not have time for that. The host jokes that he will do so after the recording anyway.

The host opens the topic of giving up on **tradition and identity** too quickly. He points out that Croatia belongs to Europe, but that even there not everything is golden. Lupino dryly replies that it is "better than the Russians". The host recalls how at 25 he considered his grandmother outdated, and today realizes that she was only trying to preserve something that was being lost.

Lupino emphasizes that for him Croatia, as far as the country itself is concerned, is the "best, best, best". In the summer he goes nowhere because summer to him is the **Adriatic Sea and Dalmatia**. In the winter he misses the sea, so then he travels to warmer parts.

The host then looks back at **anglicisms** among young people, for example "event" instead of "događaj". Lupino attributes this to internet vocabulary and admits that he does not know where this leads and how it will end, especially with artificial intelligence.

sections.subtitle: AI ne može ubiti pravu umjetnost, a novac je bio samo nusproizvod
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino govori o prodaji fotografija i novcu kao nusproizvodu
sections.content:
Na pitanje koliko će umjetna inteligencija naštetiti umjetnosti, Lupino odgovara da **pravu umjetnost neće uništiti**, jer to ne može. Površnu produkciju hoće. Osobno mu AI ne treba i čak mu je suludo o tome govoriti, pa ga izbjegava. Ljudi koji žele brzo uspjeti, smatra, moraju se služiti takvim alatima i lagati.

Voditelj ga podsjeća da je izgradio brend i ime te da su ljudi poput njega, koji su krenuli s dva kofera, svoj novac teško zaradili. Lupino ističe da u New York nije otišao zbog novca i da o tome nikad nije razmišljao. Novac je, slaže se s voditeljem, bio **nusproizvod**. Isprva nije bilo velike zarade, ali je znao da će njegovi radovi jednog dana vrijediti.

Prisjeća se kako je neke fotografije muških aktova prodavao po **9000 dolara** u **San Franciscu** i **Los Angelesu**, što nije očekivao. Uvjeren je da će njegovo djelo trajati i kad njega više ne bude.
sections.subtitle_en: AI cannot kill real art, and money was only a byproduct
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino speaks about selling photographs and money as a byproduct
sections.content_en:
To the question of how much artificial intelligence will harm art, Lupino replies that **it will not destroy real art**, because it cannot. Superficial production it will. Personally he does not need AI and to him it is even crazy to talk about it, so he avoids it. People who want to succeed quickly, he believes, have to use such tools and lie.

The host reminds him that he built a brand and a name and that people like him, who started with two suitcases, earned their money the hard way. Lupino emphasizes that he did not go to New York because of money and that he never thought about that. Money, he agrees with the host, was a **byproduct**. At first there were no big earnings, but he knew that his works would one day be valuable.

He recalls how he sold some photographs of male nudes for **9,000 dollars** in **San Francisco** and **Los Angeles**, which he did not expect. He is convinced that his work will endure even when he is no longer around.

sections.subtitle: Bi li ponovio život? Da, ali još potpuniji
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino objašnjava da umjetnik mora dati sebe u svako djelo
sections.content:
Na pitanje bi li ponovio svoj život kad bi se ponovno rodio, Lupino odgovara potvrdno. Volio bi da bude malo drugačiji i još potpuniji, jer ima još mnogo toga što bi mogao učiniti. Voditelj zaključuje da je uspio upravo zato što mu je cilj bio učiti, a ne zarađivati.

Lupino ponovno spominje studente koji ga pitaju koliko se plaća i koliko je poznat. Poručuje im da to ne pitaju. Podsjeća da je nekada fotografirao i siromahe, a profesionalni su mu modeli, priznaje, bili vrlo dosadni. Probio se, kaže, upravo fotografijama **običnih ljudi i običnih žena**.

Voditelj ističe ljepotu trenutka kad se uhvati čovjek koji ne zna da ga se fotografira. Lupino takvu fotografiju cijeni, posebno kad je rade fotografi koji idu na ratišta i bojišnice, ali njegov je pristup drukčiji. On je uvijek morao **dati nešto svoje** i izvući nešto iz modela. Kad ga pitaju kako to postiže, odgovara da to valjda nosi u sebi. Svaka umjetnost, smatra, ne postoji ako umjetnik ne da sebe. Mora biti, kaže, **„bigger than life“**.
sections.subtitle_en: Would he repeat life? Yes, but even more complete
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino explains that an artist must give themselves into every work
sections.content_en:
To the question of whether he would repeat his life if he were born again, Lupino answers affirmatively. He would like it to be a bit different and even more complete, because there is still a lot that he could do. The host concludes that he succeeded precisely because his goal was to learn, not to earn.

Lupino again mentions students who ask him how much it pays and how famous he is. He tells them not to ask that. He reminds that he once also photographed poor people, and professional models, he admits, were very boring to him. He broke through, he says, precisely with photographs of **ordinary people and ordinary women**.

The host emphasizes the beauty of the moment when a person is captured who does not know that they are being photographed. Lupino values such photography, especially when done by photographers who go to war zones and front lines, but his approach is different. He always had to **give something of his own** and draw something out of the model. When people ask him how he achieves that, he replies that he probably carries it inside himself. Any art, he considers, does not exist if the artist does not give themselves. It must be, he says, **"bigger than life"**.

sections.subtitle: Osam sati čekanja na kišu: anegdota o amateru Cibulki
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj prepričava anegdotu o fotografu amateru koji je satima čekao kišu
sections.content:
Voditelj se prisjeća fotografa amatera po imenu **Cibulka**, kojeg opisuje kao divnog čovjeka koji je živio za fotografiju. Imao je pravilo da mora fotografirati svakoga tko uđe u njegov stan, a fotografije bi poslije slao u ogromnim količinama.

Cibulka mu je jednom pokazao fotografiju na kojoj laik vidi tek jednu kap. Na njoj je zapravo bio automobil koji prolazi kroz lokvu, ali fotografa je zanimala samo ta kap. Za taj je kadar, rekao je, **čekao osam sati da padne kiša**, a zatim da automobil prođe u mraku.

Lupino ističe da jako cijeni takve fotografe, primjerice one koji snimaju životinje, jer za to treba velika strpljivost. Odaje priznanje i **ratnim fotografima**, poput onih koji rade u **Gazi**. Voditelj se prisjeća i poznate fotografije vukovarske djevojčice u kaputu. Lupino takav pristup naziva **„technical photography“**.

Upozorava da takva fotografija nestaje zbog mobitela i potrebe da se sve odmah objavi na **Instagramu**. Nekada je trebalo dan ili dva da fotografija bude gotova, a danas se sve odmah provuče kroz filtere i izgleda dobro.
sections.subtitle_en: Eight hours of waiting for rain: an anecdote about amateur Cibulka
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host recounts an anecdote about an amateur photographer who waited hours for rain
sections.content_en:
The host recalls an amateur photographer named **Cibulka**, whom he describes as a wonderful man who lived for photography. He had a rule that he had to photograph everyone who entered his apartment, and would later send the photographs in huge quantities.

Cibulka once showed him a photograph in which a layperson sees just a single drop. In it was actually a car passing through a puddle, but the photographer was interested only in that drop. For that shot, he said, **he waited eight hours for rain to fall**, and then for a car to pass in the dark.

Lupino emphasizes that he greatly values such photographers, for example those who shoot animals, because that requires great patience. He also pays tribute to **war photographers**, like those who work in **Gaza**. The host also recalls the well-known photograph of the Vukovar girl in a coat. Lupino calls such an approach **"technical photography"**.

He warns that such photography is disappearing because of mobile phones and the need for everything to be posted immediately on **Instagram**. Once it took a day or two for a photograph to be finished, and today everything is immediately run through filters and looks good.

sections.subtitle: Nestaju fotoaparati, stolari i bravari, ali njihovo znanje živi u njegovim skulpturama
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino govori o izumiranju zanata i znanju koje primjenjuje u umjetnosti
sections.content:
Voditelj pita što će biti s pravom fotografijom. Lupino se nada da neće izumrijeti, ali primjećuje da se ni aparati više ne rade kao nekad. Voditelj spominje nekadašnje velike marke poput **Nikona** i **Canona**. Lupino kaže da ih još ima, ali da je fotografija izgubila svoju težinu.

To isto vidi i u **zanatima**: stolarija, bravarija i slični zanati nestaju jer više nema ljudi koji ih rade. Voditelj se šali da mladi više ni ne znaju što je cimerman. Lupino je zahvalan što je od nekolicine majstora, koji su se razumjeli u bravariju i stolariju, naučio dovoljno da to danas primjenjuje u svojoj umjetnosti.

Prisjeća se kako su ga na početku kritizirali da se materijali „tako ne miješaju“. Danas ga isti ljudi traže da im se potpiše. Drvo je, primjerice, obrađivao na svoj način, s malo ulja, a mnogo je toga naučio u **New Yorku** dok je uređivao svoj loft. Majstori su izumrli, ali dio njihova znanja, kaže, ostao je u njemu i sada ga primjenjuje.
sections.subtitle_en: Cameras, carpenters, and locksmiths are disappearing, but their knowledge lives in his sculptures
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino speaks about the dying out of trades and the knowledge he applies in art
sections.content_en:
The host asks what will happen with real photography. Lupino hopes that it will not die out, but observes that cameras are no longer made like they used to be either. The host mentions former big brands like **Nikon** and **Canon**. Lupino says they are still around, but that photography has lost its weight.

He sees that same thing in **trades**: carpentry, locksmithing, and similar trades are disappearing because there are no longer people who do them. The host jokes that young people don't even know what a carpenter is anymore. Lupino is grateful that from a handful of craftsmen, who understood locksmithing and carpentry, he learned enough to apply it today in his art.

He recalls how at the beginning they criticized him that materials "are not mixed like that". Today the same people ask him for an autograph. Wood, for example, he treated in his own way, with a little oil, and he learned a lot of that in **New York** while decorating his loft. Craftsmen have died out, but a part of their knowledge, he says, remained in him and now he applies it.

sections.subtitle: Savjet mladim fotografima: izučite zanat, a fotografija neka bude hobi
sections.screenshot_description: Lupino daje iskren savjet mladim fotografima na kraju razgovora
sections.content:
Na pitanje što bi poručio mladom fotografu, Lupino je neočekivano izravan: neka radi nešto drugo, jer **od fotografije neće moći živjeti**. Roditeljima koji ga pitaju za savjet o sinu koji želi biti fotograf preporučuje da dijete radije ide na pravi studij ili izuči nešto drugo.

Koliko god voli fotografiju, kaže, ona je izgubila težinu jer danas ima previše fotografa. Voditelj prigovara da se pravi talent uvijek prepozna. Lupino odgovara da poznaje mnoge fotografe koji danas tek povremeno snime nekoj djevojci fotografije za Instagram.

Zamoljen za pozitivnu poruku, poručuje mladima da idu u keramičare i električare. Voditelj dodaje i vodoinstalatere te zaključuje da fotografija neka im bude hobi i strast. Lupino to potvrđuje, uz napomenu da je, nažalost, tako.

Voditelj zahvaljuje gostu i šali se da će Lupino ipak malo sjesti u kafić. Razgovor završava zajedničkom fotografijom i pozdravom gledateljima.
sections.subtitle_en: Advice to young photographers: learn a trade, and let photography be a hobby
sections.screenshot_description_en: Lupino gives candid advice to young photographers at the end of the conversation
sections.content_en:
To the question of what he would tell a young photographer, Lupino is unexpectedly direct: let him do something else, because **he will not be able to make a living from photography**. To parents who ask him for advice about a son who wants to be a photographer, he recommends that the child rather go for real studies or learn something else.

As much as he loves photography, he says, it has lost weight because today there are too many photographers. The host objects that real talent is always recognized. Lupino replies that he knows many photographers who today only occasionally take photos for Instagram for some girl.

Asked for a positive message, he tells young people to go into tiling and electrical work. The host adds plumbers as well and concludes that photography should be their hobby and passion. Lupino confirms this, noting that, unfortunately, that is how it is.

The host thanks the guest and jokes that Lupino will sit a little in a cafe after all. The conversation ends with a joint photograph and a greeting to the viewers.

iterations.theme_en: Stephan Lupino: from Rome and New York to Lupinism – photography, art, fame, and the Croatian mentality
